title: Bulk TiC geometry optimization
action: Optimize the lattice constant of bulk rocksalt TiC using plane-wave DFT with the GGA-PBE exchange-correlation functional and an open-source pseudopotential DFT code (e.g., Quantum ESPRESSO). Save the relaxed total energy, lattice vectors, and atomic positions as a plain-text output file.
description: Raw DFT output from the bulk geometry optimization. Checker parses it to extract the equilibrium lattice constant.
output_schema: Quantum ESPRESSO pw.x output file (text) containing the final lattice parameter (alat) or cell vectors from which the cubic lattice constant can be computed, and the final total energy.

title: Bulk total density of states calculation
action: Using the optimized bulk geometry, perform a static SCF calculation followed by a non-self-consistent (NSCF) calculation on a dense k-point grid to compute the total density of states. Extract the DOS data on a fine energy grid spanning approximately -20 to 20 eV relative to the Fermi energy and write it as a two-column text file (energy in eV, total DOS in states/eV/atom).
description: Two-column text file containing the total density of states for bulk TiC. Checker interpolates at the Fermi level (E=0 eV) to obtain the DOS value.
output_schema: Whitespace-separated two-column text file with no header. Column 1: energy (eV) relative to the Fermi energy. Column 2: total DOS in units of states/eV/atom.

title: Construct TiC(001) slab models
action: Using the optimized bulk lattice constant, construct symmetric TiC(001) slab supercells with 5 and 7 atomic layers terminated by the same atomic species on both sides, and include a vacuum region of at least 20 Å perpendicular to the surface. Prepare input files for geometry relaxation using the same DFT functional and code.
description: Process step to prepare slab geometries; not scored but required for downstream relaxations.

title: Relax 5-layer TiC(001) slab
action: Perform a geometry relaxation of the 5-layer slab, allowing all atomic coordinates to relax while keeping the in-plane lattice parameters fixed to the bulk value. Save the final total energy in a text file.
description: DFT output file containing the final total energy of the relaxed 5-layer slab. Used in combination with the 7-layer total energy to compute surface energy.

title: Relax 7-layer TiC(001) slab and extract surface properties
action: Perform a geometry relaxation of the 7-layer slab under the same conditions as the 5-layer slab. Save the final total energy and the relaxed atomic positions.
description: Raw DFT output from the 7-layer slab relaxation. Checker uses the final total energy (together with the evidence file slab5_relax.out) to compute the surface energy, and analyzes the atomic positions to calculate interlayer spacing changes (Δ12, Δ23, Δ34) for C and Ti layer pairs.
output_schema: Quantum ESPRESSO pw.x output file (text) containing the final total energy and the final atomic positions (in fractional or Cartesian coordinates) for the 7-layer slab.

title: Compile final structured results
action: Compute the following quantities using the raw DFT outputs: (1) the bulk lattice constant from step1, (2) the total DOS at the Fermi level from step2, (3) the surface energy for the 7-layer slab using the total energies of the relaxed 5-layer (step4 evidence) and 7-layer (step5) slabs and the known surface area, (4) the interlayer relaxation percentages Δ12, Δ23, Δ34 for C and Ti layer pairs from the relaxed atomic positions of step5. Assemble these quantities into a single JSON file following the specified schema.
description: Structured summary of the reproduction results. Checker verifies that the values in this file are consistent with those recomputed from the raw DFT outputs (steps 1, 2, 5) and awards a small reward for faithful reporting.
output_schema: JSON object with keys: 'bulk_lattice_constant' (float, Å), 'surface_energy_7layer' (float, J/m²), 'total_DOS_at_Fermi' (float, states/eV/atom), 'interlayer_spacings' (array of objects, each with 'species' (string, 'C' or 'Ti'), 'layer_pair' (string, '12','23','34'), 'delta_percent' (float)).
